To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
T cells and APCs are able to form a membrane domain that excludes the cytoplasmic components of the TCR and that this domain is required for the formation of the T cell immunological synapse.
TCRs and CD28 are organized in different membrane domains, that these domains are dynamic, and that the TCRs are in an inactive state in the resting T cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the immune response.
understanding the molecular basis of cell adhesion, cell motility and cell migration, with particular emphasis on the role of the actin cytoskeleton and its regulation by Rho-family small GTPases.
the role of membrane lipid composition in the function of the TCR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the immunological synapses of T cells are highly dynamic structures with a complex composition and that they are not static but rather are constantly changing and evolving.
there is an immunological synapse, but that it is a dynamic and flexible structure.

the TCRs of T cells are kept resting by a combination of membrane microdomains, which are in a dynamic equilibrium with the bulk of the plasma membrane, and a variety of inhibitory receptors that can be triggered by self-antigens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the T cell has evolved a mechanism for measuring the strength of TCR interactions with MHC-peptide, and this measurement is accomplished by a process that is highly sensitive and specific for the T cell receptor.
the membrane domains of the immunological synapses are important for T cell activation.
the T cell has a number of mechanisms to keep itself resting and ready to react to an APC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T cell has the ability to sense and integrate information about the number and strength of interactions with the MHC-peptide ligand.
the T cell has evolved to maintain a resting state that is ready for activation by the APC.
the T cell membrane is a complex system with multiple domains.
